definition: Human strength refers to positive capacities or advantages in people. In this source, the term is used ethically to frame neurological diversity as something that can contribute valuable abilities and resilience rather than being seen only as pathology.

reasons: The packet does not define “human strength” as “positive capacities or advantages in people”; it only contains the phrase “celebrating neurological diversity as a source of human strength,” without stating a definitional meaning.

The definition’s claim that the term is “used ethically to frame neurological diversity as something that can contribute valuable abilities and resilience rather than being seen only as pathology” is only partially supported: the packet mentions moving away from “pathological models” and celebrating diversity, but it does not explicitly mention “resilience” or “valuable abilities” as part of the term’s defined sense.
The definition adds unsupported claims such as resilience and a general gloss of “positive capacities or advantages in people,” which are not stated in the source packet.
The packet supports a narrower phrasing: neurological diversity is described as a source of human strength, but not as a general ethical definition of human strength itself.
